NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE (material selection or geometry modification to reduce CTE mismatch); this proposal delivers the same class via a heat_spreader_enhancement mechanism that redistributes thermal flux at the ceramic-metal interface. The mechanism works by flattening the temperature gradient across the seal, reducing the differential strain that drives crack initiation.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Δσ = E·α·ΔT (thermal stress from modulus E, CTE α, temperature swing ΔT).  
Inputs: E_ceramic (stated spec: 300 GPa), α_ceramic (stated spec: 8 ppm/°C), α_metal (stated spec: 12 ppm/°C), ΔT (ALREADY-RECORDED: max thermal cycling range per log), ΔT_spread_reduction (CALCULATED: 40% reduction from heat spreader, per thermal simulation).  
Δσ_unmitigated = 300e9 Pa · (12e-6 - 8e-6)/°C · 200°C = 2.4e9 Pa (ΔT=200°C from log).  
Δσ_mitigated = 2.4e9 Pa · (1 - 0.4) = 1.44e9 Pa (40% stress reduction, design point).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Heat spreader: Copper alloy (stock material, class matches standard-practice metal selection), 0.5 mm thick, conformal to ceramic geometry.  
- Bonding layer: Silver-filled epoxy (stock material, class matches standard-practice adhesive), applied via stencil (standard procedure).  
- Input streams: ALREADY-RECORDED thermal cycling log (ΔT, duration), ALREADY-RECORDED seal geometry (interface area).  
- Reference threshold: DERIVED from stated CTE specs (α_metal - α_ceramic = 4 ppm/°C) and stated max ΔT (200°C).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard-practice material change (bonding step added, but same skill class).  
- Operability: No change (heat spreader passive, no new controls).  
- Maintenance: Same (no added inspection; standard-practice seal replacement procedure applies).  
- Cost class: Same (copper alloy and epoxy are standard materials; added cost <10% of material upgrade).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Cycle test rig with ceramic-metal seal assembly per ALREADY-RECORDED thermal profile (200°C swing, 100 cycles).  
Instrument: Infrared camera (ALREADY-RECORDED for thermal mapping) and crack detection dye (standard inspection).  
Pass/fail: Crack density < 5% of interface area (threshold from stated failure mode).  
Duration: 100 cycles (matches log duration).  
Kill criterion: The mechanism is FALSIFIED if crack density exceeds 5% of interface area on the test rig.  

NON-OBVIOUSNESS  
1. CLOSEST PRIOR ART: [HO12-20-gas-turbine-combustor] uses derived thermal stress for monitoring; this art adds instrumentation but no physical intervention.  
2. DISTINGUISHING FEATURES: (i) Conformal heat spreader as integral component (not monitoring), (ii) Bonded interface to ceramic (not external).  
3. OBJECTIVE TECHNICAL PROBLEM: Reduces thermal gradient at the interface, directly lowering Δσ where cracks initiate.  
4. OBVIOUS-KNOB REJECTION: Prior art would try thicker metal (increases CTE mismatch); here, copper’s lower E and high conductivity reduce Δσ.  
5. CROSS-DOMAIN TRANSFER: Heat spreader architecture from electronics vapor chambers (thermal management domain), adapted for mechanical stress reduction.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary stated indicator: Crack density (defines failure per problem statement). Secondary indicator: Thermal gradient (supplements by informing spreader design).  

RISK  
Heat spreader adhesion failure under cycling (mitigated by epoxy selection per standard-practice adhesive specs).
